title: Neglected Projects
content:
<p>The name of my company is &quot;Ideas Never Cease&quot; (!NC) because with me, it&#39;s
true. Ideas, never <em>ever</em> cease. I am unable to turn my mind off and it has
been this way since I was eight. At 29 now, stopping isn&#39;t remotely possible
and I like that.</p>
<p>The downside, of course, is that…ideas never cease. This means I get super
focused on a great idea and work on it for some time and <em>juuuuust</em> when
things are starting to get interesting, I get distracted by another great idea
and the cycle continues. What does <em>not</em> continue, obviously, is progress on
those previous ideas…until six months to a full year later. Sometimes, even
longer than that!</p>
<p>📸<a href="https://%F0%9F%94%A5.pixels.wtf/blog/image/2017/neglected-projects-a.jpg">The notebook my fiancé bought for me</a></p>
<p>My fiancé recently bought me a dot grid notebook because it has gold and
marble on the cover, which matches my laptop<a href="/2017-01-07-macbook-pro-review.txt">1</a> a bit. I decided to use that
notebook to keep track of my weekly duties and the thought occurred to me to
write down my neglected projects. Then I figured I&#39;d share with the world
because, why not? I&#39;ve been busy with redesigning BeautyLynk<a href="https://beautylynk.com">2</a> and building
BeachfrontDigital<a href="https://beachfront.digital">3</a> so that&#39;s my excuse for not working on these projects.</p>
<p>📸<a href="https://%F0%9F%94%A5.pixels.wtf/blog/image/2017/neglected-projects-b.jpg">Some of my neglected projects</a></p>
<h2>DSGN</h2>
<p>I want to start a small web design and development firm so I can make 1) my
own hours and 2) more money so I can spend more time on passion projects that
I <em>really</em> want to work on and not expect a profit from them. To do that, I
need to actually <em>design</em> and code the new website<a href="https://dsgn.io">4</a>.</p>
<p>The good news is that BeautyLynk and BeachfrontDigital will make great initial
case studies.</p>
<h2>FRSH×BTS</h2>
<p>Man, I haven&#39;t created music in <em>years</em>. My claim to fame is that when I
released &quot;Music from the Love Lounge Vol. 1&quot;, people in Barcelona/Belize were
jamming to it. Or at the very least, one person and their friend was.
&quot;FRSH×BTS&quot; is the production name I go by, &quot;the Wibby&quot; and &quot;Spaceman Fresh&quot;
being my rap aliases.</p>
<p>I have my music on Bandcamp<a href="https://thewibby.bandcamp.com">5</a> at the moment because I never got around to
creating the perfect website for <code>frsh.fm</code>. In addition to that, I want to
remaster <em>all</em> my old work. This means getting a Windows machine, installing
Windows 7 and Acid Pro, inspecting the arrangements, and replicating them in
Studio One. I have a boatload of tracks in progress that are great jump off
points for new songs and I don&#39;t want to lose those. As you can imagine,
getting my catalogue remastered is quite the undertaking.</p>
<p><em>Le sigh</em>.</p>
<p>Oh, and I still haven&#39;t released &quot;Waveform&quot;, my debut album. When I listen to
it though, the only glaring issues I hear are vocal quality and leveling.</p>
<h2>WEÖM</h2>
<p>Short for &quot;Wisdom Escapes Ordinary Minds&quot;, WEÖM<a href="https://weom.space">6</a> is a space-centric
lifestyle brand I started a few years ago. People seem to like the snapback I
designed better than the t-shirt and I can understand why. The hat is dope and
I wear it everyday!</p>
<p>📸<a href="https://%F0%9F%94%A5.pixels.wtf/blog/image/2017/neglected-projects-c.jpg">Lakeisha and Sarah wearing WEÖM gear</a></p>
<p>I have done a <em>shitty</em> job of advertising it and generating buzz. Obviously,
that&#39;s the only way I&#39;m going to sell all the stock I have but I have a hard
time being a salesperson. Ideally, someone else would be doing this for me and
taking a cut of the profits. Also, I need to design more products. Again, I
have ideas for them but haven&#39;t gone further than sketches.</p>
<h2>!NC</h2>
<p>I created a web browser, dubbed &quot;Aries&quot;, a few years ago just to see if I
could do it and it actually worked. Not only that, but people reached out to
me to tell me how much they liked the design and how it worked. Then…I moved
onto another project. I was using Opera as my main browser back then and now
I&#39;m using Vivaldi but I still have plenty of interesting ideas to challenge
the way we think of desktop web browsers.</p>
<p>📸<a href="https://%F0%9F%94%A5.pixels.wtf/blog/image/2017/neglected-projects-d.png">Aries screenshot</a></p>
<p>&quot;Hermes&quot; is the name I&#39;m giving the desktop email client I intend to work on
at some point. Back when the latest iPhone was 5, I used a neat mobile email
app called &quot;SquareOne Mail<a href="https://techcrunch.com/2014/03/05/squareone-for-iphone-organizes-your-email-gives-you-better-control-over-notifications">7</a>&quot; and I friggin&#39; <em>loved</em> it. You could train the
app to put your email into categories you created so only the <em>most</em> important
messages appeared in your inbox. I&#39;ve heard that Gmail can do something
similar with filters but I run my own email server. The team behind SquareOne
got investors and were persuaded to pivot into something (IMHO quite)
boring…I don&#39;t even remember what it was. Anyhoo, Hermes would be an evolved
version of the original.</p>
<h2>SciLab</h2>
<p>I&#39;ve saved the best for last. Prepare for a lot of backstory.</p>
<p>If you follow me on social media or other online networks, you may have
wondered at some point what a &quot;NetOp&quot; or &quot;NetOperator&quot; is. Well, that comes
from a beloved video game series, called &quot;Megaman Battle Network&quot; (MMBN).
There are six main games in the series and the timeline is set in the year
20XX…yes, like other Megaman games. In this future, everyone has an A.I.
companion called an &quot;Internet Navigator&quot;, or &quot;NetNavi&quot; for short. The people
who operate these A.I.s are often referred to as NetOperators. So, combined
with my rap alias you read earlier, NetOperator Wibby became my online handle
of choice.</p>
<p>Also in this future? A 3D Internet and a futuristic device (Personal Terminal,
or PET) that is basically a smartphone. Not so revolutionary-sounding but when
the first game came out (2001), it was mind-blowing and captured my
imagination. Can you see where I&#39;m going with this? <em>The ideas never ceased.</em></p>
<p>It became quite clear to me that this awesome-sounding future had to exist
because…reasons. Like…it&#39;s awesome. But, how was <em>I</em> going to make this
happen? I was only 13 at the time with a <em>lot</em> of time on my hands.
<em>Good grief, I spent 16 years thinking about this stuff</em> 😰</p>
<p>When I (briefly) attended college, I enrolled in Software Engineering for the
<em>sole purpose</em> of learning how to write an operating system, even if it was
from a middle-aged man with <em>impeccable</em> bright white facial hair and a
tendency to accidentally spit on students in the front row. However, I was
forced to leave because I found out I couldn&#39;t afford college. That dashed my
dreams a bit but I taught myself web design and development, got an
apprenticeship, and eventually landed good-paying jobs and skills that led me
to think, &quot;What if I just…<em>wrote</em> an &#39;operating system&#39; in HTML/CSS/JS?&quot;. This
is how <em>hikari OS<a href="https://hikar.io">8</a></em> was born! For those keeping score at home, &quot;hikari&quot; is
the creator of the 3D Internet and NetNavis in MMBN. Hey, innovation is a
family business.</p>
<p><em>hikari is an Electron app that will be designed to boot from a minimal Linux
distro in fullscreen on a Raspberry Pi.</em> It&#39;s like Chrome OS in a way. Anyhoo,
I worked on hikari for awhile and got distracted, of course.</p>
<p>For my NetNavi project, I&#39;d need a good voice recognition/synthesis library
and currently, Google is the best for that and I don&#39;t consider them an option
because they are beyond terrible with user privacy. I&#39;m not sure why they need
to store your voice commands on their servers for an unspecified amount of
time but hey, that&#39;s what happens when things are free. I&#39;m not expecting my
NetNavi project to be considered &quot;real A.I.&quot;. Siri, Cortana, and everything
else are just elaborate <code>if</code>/<code>then</code>/<code>else</code> statements. The PET is low priority
because the base being a Raspberry Pi makes things super easy (like, creating
a dock station, &amp;c).</p>
<p>Lastly, the 3D Internet. In my research, I got downvoted to hell across a
couple StackExchange sites (I was told to ask a different site, at least four
times). In hindsight, that&#39;s what I get for going there for useful advice.</p>
<p>With regard to &quot;NetCity&quot; in the MMBN anime, I sketched a process that would
allow for the automatic generation of buildings based on how deep a website&#39;s
links went. Take this site for example! I have four main links in the header.
Each of those links would represent a different floor. Each page&#39;s contents
would be represented on each floor depending on what it was. Blog posts would
become eBooks, mp3s would become a CD, and so on. Just like search engine bots
visit your website every now and then, so would this 3D &#39;Net bot and it would
report changes that would update your generated building.</p>
<p>This 3D &#39;Net would be accessed via &quot;the Network&quot;, which is effectively an
MMORPG where your NetNavi is your avatar. Aries would have a built-in viewer
for this, although I&#39;d probably just use three.js.</p>
<p>…This is going off the rails, I understand that. This is also going to cost a
<em>fuck</em> ton of money. Yes, the fuck was necessary because unless I become super
rich in the next 10 years, what I&#39;m seeing in my head will never see the light
of day until I&#39;m 60…y&#39;know what, that&#39;s around the age Grandpa Hikari created
the Internet. Also, I just realized that he looks like a chubby Vint Cerf.</p>
<h2>&amp;c</h2>
<p>I could go on and on about my project backlog. Here&#39;s a couple more that are
in the incubation stage of my ideation process:</p>
<ul>
<li>social network that doesn&#39;t suck, enables better communication, provides
ways for users to deal with harassment, and makes money without selling user
data.</li>
<li>an outlet that showcases black excellence, positivity, and training
resources to aid small business owners and aspiring freelancers.</li>
<li>an eCommerce platform that allows for true customization, doesn&#39;t treat you
like you&#39;re dumb, and has a self-hosted option.</li>
<li>a curated site for lefties that doesn&#39;t look like it was built in 1999 and
stayed that way.</li>
</ul>
<p>I&#39;ll get to these projects some day. I&#39;ve attempted to work on things on a
schedule but my mind/enthusiasm doesn&#39;t work that way. I&#39;m using a dot grid
notebook as a weekly planner instead of the weekly planner I bought months
ago, simply because predefined lines and boxes make me feel constrained. I&#39;m
not quite sure what the solution is but I think if I had more time (hah, don&#39;t
we all want this?) and made my own hours, I could figure this thing out. Or at
the very least, start knocking things out one by one. 🕸</p>
